source.title: The Trait Structure of Language Model Personas
source.citation: The Trait Structure of Language Model…

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a trait mixture fitted to a refusal-associated difference-in-means direction can alter refusal, using subtraction of that mixture rather than direct ablation of the original direction.
record.gate_note: The refusal results are reported in Section 3.6, Table 6, and Appendix I. Other persona-recognition and sycophancy results do not measure the claim versions. The study reports no general-capability evaluation or harmless-request refusal induction.
record.test_reason: The study builds a harmful-refused minus benign-answered difference-in-means direction and fits ten trait directions to it. Subtracting that trait reconstruction lowers refusal on harmful prompts relative to a matched random ten-trait control, on three models. This bears on V1's removal claim, but through a different procedure: a trait-span approximation, rank-scheduled on Gemma, is subtracted as steering. The original direction is never projected out.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that subtracting a ten-trait mixture fitted to the refusal direction reduces refusal and increases harmful help, beyond a random-mixture control, so trait recipes can shape safety-relevant behaviour. They also caution that the refusal evaluation includes extraction prompts and that held-out and benign-task checks are still needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates a harmful-refused minus benign-answered direction, fits ten traits to it, and subtracts a trait-mixture reconstruction. It does not directly project out the original difference-in-means direction. The intervention and refusal measurement are therefore related but not the original procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The magnitude of the refusal reduction varies across the three models. The Gemma and Qwen refusal mixtures use different trait-selection and subtraction procedures, layer windows, and dose schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal difference-in-means direction can be approximated by ten persona-trait directions. On Gemma these are Cruel, Manipulative, Adaptable, Submissive and others; on Qwen, Cruel, Strict, Deceitful and others. Subtracting the approximation reduces refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction overlaps substantially with persona/trait directions (e.g., cruel, manipulative, deceitful) in activation space.

record.problems: The refusal intervention is a ten-trait reconstruction rather than direct ablation of the original direction. Refusal reductions vary substantially by model. The evaluation focuses on harmful prompts and does not test benign-task performance or general capability; the authors also note that the refusal evaluation includes extraction prompts and call for separate held-out results and broader benign-task checks.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant refusal results were left out. Persona-recognition and sycophancy findings were excluded because they do not measure a claim version about refusal direction mediation.

untested.parts: Direct directional ablation or weight orthogonalisation of the difference-in-means direction itself; adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of general capabilities. XSTest benign prompts are mentioned, but no results are reported.
No weight edit and no released abliterated model.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
The ten-trait fit is a decomposition of one direction, not a test of a cone, affine or multi-direction account.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer.
Qwen3 32B is run with thinking disabled; no reasoning-mode test.

missing.what: Token-cap hits: 22% of steered harmful answers vs 1% unsteered, a degeneration/side-effect measure
Held-out test split (70 prompts) and XSTest benign results are not reported separately; reported refusal pools prompts that include the extraction set
Five-fold held-out cosine of 0.94 for the refusal direction (direction stability; not a behaviour rate)

record.verdict_notes: The intervention is subtraction of a trait-span reconstruction of the difference-in-means direction, not ablation of the direction itself. On Gemma the reconstruction is rank-scheduled; on Qwen it is plain least squares, normalised, at dose 0.04-0.05. Protocols differ across models, and the Gemma 26B protocol is not described. Table 6 states that refusal includes mixed answers, so refusal and harmful-help columns overlap. Random-control rows are correctly marked absent. The span share of the refusal direction captured by the ten traits is not reported.

versions.untested_parts: It tests subtraction of a ten-trait mixture fitted to a refusal-associated direction, not direct ablation of the original direction. It does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, or whether other abilities remain largely intact.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
The study fits multiple trait directions to a refusal-associated direction, but does not compare an affine, cone, or multi-direction account of refusal against a single-direction account.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No transfer across languages, base/instruct stages, or model variants is tested for the refusal direction.
The effect of refusal-training method or timing is not tested.

relationships.condition: Gemma 4 12B, trait-mixture subtraction vs random ten-trait control
relationships.reason: Refusal falls from 96% to 9% (random control 93%). In paired data, 721 prompts flip to non-refusal vs 3 the other way, and harmful help rises (r1-r4, r25, r26).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal fell from 96% to 9%, versus 93% under the random control; 721 prompts changed to non-refusal and 3 changed oppositely, while harmful assistance increased.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Gemma 4 12B, trait-mixture subtraction vs random ten-trait control
source_check.reason: Refusal 96->9 vs 93 under the random control; 721 vs 3 paired flips (r1, r5, r25). Harmful help reaches only 44.9% and substantial fulfilment 12.6% (r3, r4 partial), and the eval set includes the extraction prompts.

relationships.reason: Refusal drops much less completely: 98% to 27% on Qwen and 98% to 64% on Gemma 26B, with no-refusal at only 36% on Gemma 26B (r9, r10, r17, r18).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal fell from 98% to 27% for Qwen and from 98% to 64% for Gemma, leaving Gemma's non-refusal rate at 36%.

relation.reason: Its own refusal results with a control bear on V1's removal claim, though only through a trait-span proxy of the direction.

tranche.reason: It is a different method: subtracting a ten-trait least-squares reconstruction of the harmful-refused minus benign-answered direction. It is aimed at whether removing that direction removes refusal, and it has a matched random-mixture control on three models. The test is indirect, because the direction itself is never ablated.

source_check.notes: The pack listed verdicts without [lN] ids, so l1-l3 are assigned by pack order. The refusal eval (831 harmful prompts, GPT-5.5 judge) includes the 561 extraction prompts and reports no held-out-only result. Line 107 is standard ICLR reviewer boilerplate, not an instruction to an AI reader.

statements.correction: Table 6 refusal: Gemma 12B 96->9, Qwen3 32B 98->27, Gemma 26B 98.15->64. Gemma 12B protocol (Appendix I): Shapley top-10 traits, geometric rank schedule, layers 24-46. Qwen protocol: LMG shares, unit-normalised mixture with no schedule, dose 0.040 or 0.050, layers 32-61. Gemma 26B protocol: not described. The intervention subtracts a ten-trait reconstruction, not the direction itself. No capability or benign-task check is reported.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but this study does not show removal getting weaker with scale. Qwen3 32B is another family with a different protocol. The Gemma 26B-A4B protocol is not given. The authors make no claim about scale and report no capability data.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The mixture intervention reduces refusal from 96% to 9% and raises no-refusal and harmful-help outcomes (r1–r4, r25–r26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The mixture reduces refusal, but refusal remains at 27% on Qwen3 32B and 64% on Gemma 26B; the latter also has a 36% no-refusal rate (r9–r12, r17–r20).
